decisionEvidence.observed: DEQ found 2025 application incomplete for missing recognized top-down Best Available Control Technology analysis; BACT addendum later submitted October 6.
decisionEvidence.limit: This does not establish the plant construction start or physical operation.

decisionEvidence.observed: Applicant asked whether one third of identical furnaces could be tested initially; DEQ retained initial source testing of all new furnace units because antimony is a hazardous air pollutant.
decisionEvidence.limit: Source-testing regulatory requirement does not verify results, operation, completion, due dates or violations.

decisionEvidence.observed: Commenter asserted company announcements from 2021–2025 suggested earlier furnace installation/operation and questioned whether those installations preceded this permit.
decisionEvidence.limit: This is an allegation using older press releases, not an independent finding of pre-permit illegal operation or proof of new 2025 expansion-unit commissioning.

decisionEvidence.issuer: Power Engineers on behalf of US Antimony
decisionEvidence.observed: Applicant said this action adds new furnace units, upgrades existing baghouses and decommissions two older units; it characterized previous installations as within prior permit limits, and described some older trisulfide furnaces as lab-scale electric equipment outside the air-permit requirement.
decisionEvidence.limit: Two units being decommissioned is a company statement of planned/in-progress change, not a verified physical retirement date or reconciliation of the reported six-versus-seven legacy unit count.

followUp: Use both application Table 2 unit IDs and matching baghouse IDs in existing May–October 2026 Montana DEQ source-test/inspection requests. Ask for completed 2026 records and equipment status; no second request has yet been submitted or received.
